reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern consists of a quasi-periodic pulse train with a fundamental period of ~98 points, as confirmed by the reference_cycle_plan and estimated_period. Each cycle features a sharp, near-vertical rise (duration ~2–4 points) to a peak between 15–19 robust-standardized units, followed by a rapid drop (~3–6 points) to near-zero baseline, then a low-amplitude noisy plateau lasting ~80–90 points before the next pulse. Baseline is stable near zero (median ≈ 0), with minor drift (<0.01 per point) across longer windows. Peak morphology is consistent: slightly asymmetric with steeper ascent than descent, rounded tops (not尖锐 spikes), and minimal pre-peak oscillation. Troughs are flat and shallow (≈0–1), occasionally dipping slightly negative but rarely below −1. Noise during baseline is low-magnitude (MAD ≈ 0.66–0.67), irregular, and non-Gaussian—appearing as small jagged fluctuations without clear structure. Amplitude_90 is tightly clustered (17.4–19.1), indicating high amplitude consistency. Roughness (~0.166) and curvature (~0.168–0.171) are nearly identical across candidates, confirming morphological stability. Minor variations exist in exact peak height and baseline offset (e.g., ref 0 has median 0.65, others near 0), but these are attributable to local trend or normalization artifacts rather than true anomaly. No sustained trends or regime shifts are present; all candidates exhibit the same pulse cadence and shape when aligned by cycle count.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer reference 1 or 2 for query segments with 2–4 cycles due to highest morphological fidelity and lowest noise. Use reference 3 when analyzing longer windows (>400 pts) where slow drift or amplitude modulation may be relevant. Reference 0 is suitable only for single-pulse validation or boundary-effect analysis; avoid for multi-cycle comparison due to truncation and elevated baseline. When query shows asymmetric pulses or baseline offsets, compare against ref 1/2 first—ref 3’s drift may mislead if not accounted for.
uncertainties: Exact pulse onset timing tolerance (±1–2 pts) not quantified
Whether minor amplitude decay in ref 3 is systematic or stochastic
Potential for very short-duration anomalies (<3 pts) to be masked by pulse rise/fall slopes
Robust-standardized scale obscures absolute magnitude context; true physical meaning of '18' units unknown
